issues.description: SealSaloon.stock attribute: The problem statement first instructs that a final Stock field named 'stock' should be initialized to a default value in the SealSaloon constructor (i.e., instance initialization in the no-arg constructor). Later in the same problem statement it requires that the 'stock' attribute must be static (shared across all instances) and that acceptSupplyDelivery and calculateTotalPrice be static as well. The provided reference solution declares the field as a static final field initialized at declaration (private static final Stock stock = new Stock()). This contradiction (instance-initialized final field vs class-level static final field) confuses students about whether 'stock' should be an instance or class field and where/how it must be initialized.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent. Either (A) require a shared stock by specifying: "Declare the stock field as 'private static final Stock stock' and initialize it either at the point of declaration (e.g. = new Stock()) or in a static initializer; do not initialize it in the instance constructor," or (B) remove the 'static' requirement and state explicitly to initialize a non-static final stock in the no-arg constructor. Update problem_statement.md accordingly so it matches the reference solution and removes the conflicting instruction about constructor initialization.
